shadow:
The mind likes to know where it stands. So it picks a side and stands there. This is how an opinion forms, not from looking, but from needing a place to put your weight down.

Most opinions were laid in early, somewhere in the teenage years, around an old sting that never got named. A small hurt becomes a rule about how the world works. The rule feels like clear thinking. It is really just the hurt, grown a face and a voice.

The trouble is not having a view. The trouble starts when the view has to be guarded. Once a position must be defended, the mind goes hard around it. Conversation turns into a contest with two sides and a winner. The harder a person argues, the more there is a sore spot underneath the argument doing the talking.

And here is the thing the contest hides. The same mind that splits the world in two is the one organ in you that can read a pattern. That skill is not the enemy. It has only been pointed at the wrong target, sorting people into right and wrong instead of watching how one thing actually leads to the next.
repressive: Some people meet it by handing the verdict to everyone else. They compare themselves to whoever is in the room and quietly come out lower. They hold no opinion of their own, because somewhere they decided their own read was not worth saying.
reactive: Others meet it by going on the attack. They wield logic like a tool for proving other people wrong, and they get louder the moment a view is questioned. It looks like confidence. It is anger standing guard over a fear.
gift:
Something loosens when a person stops needing to win. The opinion does not get replaced by a better opinion. It just stops being load-bearing. You can hold a view and set it down again, and nothing about you falls over.

What opens then is far-sightedness. The pattern-reading skill, freed from defending one corner, finally gets to do its real work. It watches how this leads to that. It sees the shape a thing will take before the thing arrives. This is not vision in the dreamy sense. It is closer to a falcon's eye, the small detail caught clean from a long way off, and the long arc caught at the same time.

You stop arguing across at people and start seeing alongside them. When someone is locked tight inside their position, there is no urge to crack them open or to drown them in kindness. You let them have their process. You say your piece and leave it warm on the table.

The seeing comes in bursts. A clear stretch, then ordinary fog again. The fog is not failure. It is the gap where the last clear thing gets to settle into the body before the next one arrives.
siddhi:
At the top of this there is no longer someone doing the looking. The eye and what the eye rests on are one motion. People have called this the third eye, and pictured it in the forehead, but it is not really there. It is in every cell, and when it opens the whole body becomes the thing that sees.

This is omniscience, and it is quieter than the word sounds. Past and present and what is coming all lie on a single surface, seen at once. There is no waiting between the seeing and the answer. The falcon's hood comes off and the whole creature is already in motion.

From here a person looks back down the road. The opinion at the start, the hard little verdict built around an old wound, was never a defect to be ashamed of. It was the mind learning to read a pattern the only way it could at that frequency, by picking a side first. The splitting had to happen. It was the eye, half open, practising in the dark before the light came up.
